title: Minimum distance of a binary [109, 14] linear code
statement: A binary [109, 14, d] linear code is a 14-dimensional subspace of GF(2)^109 in which every nonzero vector has Hamming weight at least d. The largest achievable d is unknown for these parameters: codes are known with d = 45, and no code can have d greater than 48.

title: Minimum distance of a [199, 7] linear code over GF(4)
statement: A [199, 7, d] linear code over GF(4) is a 7-dimensional subspace of GF(4)^199 in which every nonzero vector has Hamming weight at least d. The largest achievable d is unknown for these parameters: codes are known with d = 140, and no code can have d greater than 145.

title: Minimum distance of a [98, 8] linear code over GF(5)
statement: A [98, 8, d] linear code over GF(5) is a 8-dimensional subspace of GF(5)^98 in which every nonzero vector has Hamming weight at least d. The largest achievable d is unknown for these parameters: codes are known with d = 69, and no code can have d greater than 73.

title: (28800, 930, 30)-difference set in Z_12 x Z_2400
statement: A (28800, 930, 30)-difference set in the abelian group Z_12 x Z_2400 is a 930-element subset D such that every nonzero group element is a difference of two members of D in exactly 30 ways. Whether one exists is unknown: the parameters pass the standard nonexistence tests, and no example is known.

title: Erdős $5000 Problem on Prime Gaps
statement: Is it true that for infinitely many $n$, $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n > c \ln n \ln \ln n \ln \ln \ln \ln n / (\ln \ln \ln n)^2$ for arbitrarily large constant $c$?
